title: Backbone or no backbone? Sorting animals
examples: Are there more animals with or without backbones?

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: Does this animal have a backbone?

explain.say: Put your hand on the middle of your back and bend forward. Can you feel bumpy bones? That is your backbone, also called your spine. Some animals have one and some do not. Let's sort them.

draw.text: Backbone or no backbone? Sorting animals

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Does this animal have a backbone?

explain.say: See the Backbone group lighting up? Animals with a backbone are called vertebrates. Dogs, snakes, frogs, eagles and salmon all have one, and so do you. A backbone holds the body up like a strong pole. Can you add one more animal here?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Does this animal have a backbone?

explain.say: Now the No backbone group glows. These are invertebrates, which means no backbone. Ants and snails have hard shells or skins outside; worms and jellyfish are soft all over. Does a spider go in this group? Yes it does!

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Does this animal have a backbone?

explain.say: Now look at the two bars. Which do you think is bigger? Here is the surprise: about 97 out of every 100 kinds of animals have no backbone! Insects alone are a huge crowd. Animals with backbones are only a tiny slice.

items.label: No backbone
items.ask: Are there more animals with or without backbones?

explain.say: Back to the No backbone group, and that octopus. It has no bones at all, so it can squeeze through a hole not much bigger than its beak. Super sorting! Next time you see a snail or an ant, you can whisper: invertebrate!

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Does this animal have a backbone?

faq.a: A vertebrate is an animal with a backbone. Mammals, birds, fish, reptiles and amphibians are all vertebrates.
An invertebrate is an animal without a backbone, such as insects, spiders, worms, snails, octopuses, crabs and jellyfish.

faq.q: Are there more animals with or without backbones?
faq.a: Far more without. About 97 percent of known animal species are invertebrates, and insects make up most of them.
No. An octopus has no bones at all. Its only hard part is its beak, so it can squeeze through tiny gaps.
asks: How does an octopus squeeze through holes?

faq.q: What holds up an animal with no backbone?
faq.a: Many have a hard outer case, like an insect or a crab, or a shell like a snail. Worms and jellyfish are held in shape by water inside them.
asks: How do insects stay in shape?

facts: About 97 percent of described animal species are invertebrates.
An octopus has no bones; its hard beak is the only rigid part of its body.

quiz.say: Which of these animals is a vertebrate?
quiz.why: A parrot is a bird, and all birds have a backbone.

wrong.0: An earthworm is soft all through, with no backbone.
wrong.1: A snail has a shell but no backbone.

quiz.say: Are most kinds of animals vertebrates or invertebrates?
quiz.why: About 97 percent of animal kinds have no backbone.

wrong.0: Vertebrates are only about 3 percent of animal kinds.
wrong.2: It is nowhere near half: invertebrates win by far.
